standard_deviation_verification.summary_convention_detected: NumPy default ddof=0 (population standard deviation) used across all original JSON result summaries.

investigation_config_c_f1_discrepancy.issue: Earlier narrative text noted Config C Macro F1 as 68.21% +/- 1.09%, while the new audit reports 68.21% +/- 1.17%.
investigation_config_c_f1_discrepancy.root_cause_explanation: The value 1.09% did not originate from Config C calculations. In Phase 3 (DP sigma=2.0), the population standard deviation (ddof=0) for Macro F1 is exactly 0.010877... (saved in JSON as 0.0109, i.e., 1.09%). An earlier draft text transposed this 1.09% value onto Config C. The true Config C Macro F1 metrics are: mean = 68.21%, population standard deviation (ddof=0) = 1.04% (0.0104), and sample standard deviation (ddof=1) = 1.17% (0.0117). Thus, 1.17% in the audit reflects the correct sample standard deviation (ddof=1), whereas 1.09% was an erroneous narrative transposition.

sigma_0.5.scientific_interpretation: At sigma=0.5, mean paired accuracy difference is +0.086 pp. Across the 5 seeds, differences correspond to integer correct-count shifts of 0 to 2 records, demonstrating negligible empirical impact of the SecAgg+ quantization layer on DP model utility.

sigma_1.0.scientific_interpretation: At sigma=1.0, mean paired accuracy difference is -0.002 pp. Across the 5 seeds, differences correspond to integer correct-count shifts of 0 to 2 records, demonstrating negligible empirical impact of the SecAgg+ quantization layer on DP model utility.

sigma_1.5.scientific_interpretation: At sigma=1.5, mean paired accuracy difference is +0.000 pp. Across the 5 seeds, differences correspond to integer correct-count shifts of 0 to 2 records, demonstrating negligible empirical impact of the SecAgg+ quantization layer on DP model utility.

sigma_2.0.scientific_interpretation: At sigma=2.0, mean paired accuracy difference is -0.028 pp. Across the 5 seeds, differences correspond to integer correct-count shifts of 0 to 2 records, demonstrating negligible empirical impact of the SecAgg+ quantization layer on DP model utility.

sampling_ratio_investigation.code_trace: In Opacus 1.6.0, DPDataLoader.from_data_loader calculates sample_rate as 1 / len(data_loader). With client dataset size 731 and batch_size 32, len(data_loader) is ceil(731/32) = 23. Consequently, Opacus sets sample_rate = 1/23 = 0.04347826, which is recorded in pe.accountant.history on each optimizer step. This yields an expected Poisson batch size of E[|B|] = 731 * (1/23) = 31.78 samples (~31.8). The privacy accountant mathematically accounts for Poisson subsampling at rate q = 1/23.

accountant_persistence_across_rounds.mechanism: client_privacy_engines list instantiated outside federated rounds loop (25 rounds). History accumulates monotonically.

privacy_scope_demarcation.record_level_dp: Applies strictly to client training samples (N=731 per client) under neighboring datasets differing by +/- 1 training observation.

test_set_isolation_verification.evaluation_timing: Strictly once at the completion of round 25 for each model training run.
test_set_isolation_verification.wording_clarification: The test set was evaluated once per completed model run (totaling 25 evaluations across the 25 benchmark runs), not evaluated during training rounds 1..24, and never used to select models or tune hyperparameters.

config_c_vs_config_a.interpretation: Config C exceeds Config A by +0.328 pp (+0.485% relative), well within empirical seed variation (sample std = 1.16 pp).

discrepancies.resolution: 32/731 was the nominal batch size ratio. Opacus implements sample_rate = 1 / len(data_loader) = 1/23. Both the runtime DPDataLoader and the Opacus accountant used q = 1/23 = 0.04347826. Expected batch size was 31.78 samples. All epsilon calculations accurately reflect q = 1/23.

discrepancies.description: Raw benchmark JSON summaries computed population std (ddof=0), while scientific reporting requires sample std (ddof=1).
discrepancies.resolution: Both conventions have been reconstructed and audited. For N=5, sample std is exactly sqrt(5/4) = 1.1180 times population std. Paper drafting will adopt sample standard deviation (ddof=1) as the primary convention, with population std explicitly documented in footnotes.

discrepancies.category: Config C Macro F1 Standard Deviation Narrative Typo
discrepancies.description: Earlier text cited Config C Macro F1 as 68.21% +/- 1.09%, while audit reports 68.21% +/- 1.17%.
discrepancies.resolution: The value 1.09% was the population std (ddof=0) of Phase 3 DP sigma=2.0 Macro F1 (0.010877... rounded to 0.0109). The true Config C Macro F1 metrics from the 5 raw seed runs are: mean = 68.21%, population std (ddof=0) = 1.04%, and sample std (ddof=1) = 1.17%. The discrepancy was an editorial narrative transposition.

discrepancies.description: Clarified scope of test evaluation frequency.
discrepancies.resolution: The test set was evaluated strictly once per completed model run at round 25 (25 evaluations total across the 25 runs), with zero evaluations during rounds 1..24 and zero usage for hyperparameter selection or early stopping.

paper_claims_supported: Empirical feasibility of defense-in-depth federated learning combining per-sample DP-SGD with SecAgg+ on wearable sensor data.
SecAgg+ quantization and Shamir-masking incur negligible utility penalty (mean accuracy difference |delta| <= 0.086 pp across all noise multipliers; +0.328 pp in plaintext).
Rigorous record-level (epsilon, delta)-DP guarantee with epsilon = 4.29 (PRV) / 4.64 (RDP) at sigma = 2.0 and delta = 1e-5 across 1,725 accounted steps.
Retained utility of 38.44% test accuracy on 6-class activity classification under epsilon = 4.29, well above random chance (16.67%).
Complete cryptographic and functional verification of custom SecAgg+ protocol against Flower 1.42 primitives under dropouts and boundary conditions.
paper_claims_not_supported: Patient-level differential privacy (the dataset lacks verified patient boundaries per record, so adjacency is strictly per-sample/record-level).
HIPAA or GDPR regulatory compliance certification (mathematical DP is not equivalent to legal compliance).
Zero information leakage across all threat models (the aggregate model update itself leaks bounded differential privacy epsilon).
Cryptographic confidentiality proven solely by utility benchmarks (utility tests verify non-distortion, not ciphertext hardness).
Zero utility degradation in general (utility drops from 67.60% to 38.44% under DP noise, even though SecAgg adds no further degradation).
Differential privacy for held-out test records (DP-SGD bounds training record privacy; test evaluation is conventional empirical testing).
Statistical equivalence proven from five seeds (five seeds demonstrate empirical consistency within integer record granularity, not asymptotic proof).

final_readiness_status.justification: All 25 Phase 4 benchmark runs, baseline metrics, paired differences, and privacy-accounting calculations have been verified from raw seed data and source code. All four documented discrepancies (sampling ratio, std convention, Config C F1 narrative typo, test set isolation scope) have been resolved. The experimental artifacts provide a complete and verified evidentiary foundation for paper drafting, subject to the negative boundary constraints in paper_claims_not_supported.
